So I tested several dozen glasses of water from over a dozen sources. TDS is any and all solids dissolved in the water. This could be harmless like salt, or hazardous like chemical runoff.

Source Factor 1 Factor 2 Bottle Size TDS Notes
Well Cold Fresh 146
Well Hot Fresh 145
Well Cold Sat for >24 hours 136
Well Hot Sat for >24 hours 143
Well Boiled/Cooled Sat for >24 hours 97 *1
Tap Taco Bell Soda Machine 74
Tap Work Building 1 63
Tap Work Building 2 59
Tap Hotel Sink 53
Tap Hotel Ice Machine 12 *2
Bottled Brand 1 Spring 16.9 oz 8
Bottled Brand 1 Spring Gal 7
Bottled Brand 1 Distilled Gal 0
Bottled Brand 2 Distilled Gal 0
Bottled Brand 3 Distilled Gal <1
Bottled Brand 1 Purified 16.9 oz 2
Bottled Brand 1 Purified Gal 3
Bottled Brand 2 Purified 16.9 oz 27 *3
Bottled Brand 2 Purified Gal 4 *3
Bottled Brand 3 Purified Gal 4
Bottled Brand 4 Baby Gal 94 *4
Rain Puddle 1 Dirt Driveway Tested next morning 6
Rain Puddle 1 Under Trees Tested next morning 8
Rain Open Field Bucket 5
Rain Roof Bucket 13 *5
Lake Cloudy 60 *6

Other Tests

No effects:

  • Letting water sit in sun
  • Filtering with Katadyn Hiker Pro (expired filter)
  • Filtering with Life Straw (not expired filter)

Effects on 1 cup of distilled water (0 TDS start point)

  • 0.5gr sea salt (~10 granules) -- 140 TDS
  • 10 drops 5% White Vinegar -- 28 TDS
  • 10 drops 5% Apple Cider Vinegar -- 28 TDS

Notes:

1) I believe this may have had something to do with the minerals depositing on the inside of the kettle.

2) Ice Machine probably has filter of some kind.

3) Note the large difference between Gallon and 16.9 oz compared to other brands

4) Note the high TDS compared to other bottled water. Perhaps it has more minerals for baby.

5) Likely collected chemicals and debris from Tar Shingles

6) Collected at surface near shoreline. Note how it's comparable to tap/well water. Mild taste.

Comments

Regardless of the TDS, some water tasted better than others. Some of the bottled water had a distinct plastic taste, including one of the distilled waters. TDS has some effect on what water tastes like, but it matters more as to what it actually is.

140 from salt /= 140 vinegar water /= 140 well water /= 94 baby water. Each one tasted way different than the others. Salt was almost unnoticeable.

Gerber Purified Baby Water had a unique taste, likely due to higher TDS content (perhaps minerals for baby). I'll look for other baby water for comparison.

Lake water tasted fine, although I wouldn't drink more than a sip or two without purifying it.

Surprisingly, neither the backpacking filter nor the lifestraw had any effect on TDS. I'd still trust them to make water safe though.

I tested bleach the same way I tested salt and vinegar, but I never wrote down the results, and I'm out of bleach. It did have a significant effect on the TDS of the water though.

Both minerals and chemicals will register as TDS. You don't need to reduce overall TDS just because. Buying a reverse osmosis water filter to help with hard water or remove fluoride is fine though.

TDS will not help with bacteria/microorganisms. I trust my well water, but I don't trust the lake or puddle water.
